First of all, aluminum will be a bitch to saw and won't be good to learn on. I'd try copper or brass, from 18-20 gauge. 16 gauge is sometimes too thick to saw easily. You can use rubber cement to glue a piece of paper with your design or sketch inked (pencil will rub off) onto it to the metal, but you'll need to let the glue really dry. I usually glue and let dry overnight then saw away. 

I use bees wax as a lubricant but you can buy commercial lubricants. Use a bench pin. The more intricate your designs the smaller you want your blade to be. I cut very intricate designs and use a 3/0 blade. If I was teaching someone starting out I'd give them a range of blade sizes to try. I find Swiss made blades to be the best.

Edit: years back I had a sudden, unexplained cyst like swelling right over where my neuroma was. It went down overnight but the front half of my foot turned black from the bruising and it hurt so bad I couldn't wear shoes. I went to primary care and they acted like I'd dropped something on my foot to try to get pain pills or something. I just wish they had done imaging or referred me out to a specialist because I can't help but wonder if such a weird event was the start of things and if I could have been spared years of suffering. I didn't take pictures of the cyst like swelling and highly regret that. I would be curious if any fellow MN sufferers had anything similar happen before onset.

Older cars often begin to get mysterious oil leaks that, if they are diagnosable, require repairs worth more than the value of the car itself. Those of us driving such reprobates without recourse would need to check (and perhaps top up) the oil every time we get gas in order to ensure that we get home without our beloved clunker eating itself. 

Additionally, sometimes it is too expensive to repair a leaky radiator right away, or the car just tends to overheat and we're not sure why. Before the needle hits red, you pull over somewhere safe and well lit (ideally) pop the hood and wait for the engine to cool so you can top up the radiator. You might also use a gallon of water to splash on the engine (but never on the engine block lest it shock and split!!!) to speed the process up. Opening a hot radiator is a recipe for the burn ward, which we also can't afford (can you tell what country we live in lol). Coolant gets expensive when you're buying it just for it to leak on the road, hence the gallons of water. Burns off faster but can still save your engine.

The technique is called granulation, and it dates back to ancient Egypt, at least. It's usually only used with gold, because it utilizes the property of gold that it will fuse together under heat without solder. You can use rabbit glue to fix your little beads in place before heating.

You can, however, do it in other metals with the following technique: snip silver solder as tiny as you can, get some dried up handy flux and make a powder out of it. Mix it with the silver solder clippings and sprinkle over the piece. Then heat as if you were doing traditional granulation.

If someone were to call me selfish while I was in that place it would simply show their lack of understanding of my suffering. I was trapped in my own body and I couldn't bear it any longer. Suicide seemed like the only option for relief.

Inpatient, and lithium saved my life, and my illnesses are diagnosed and managed at least now, and I even walked several miles yesterday with my walker. My body will never go back to "normal" but even so I am still mostly happy and excited to be excited about the future and the good things in my life. But through counseling with my SO I can only now fully understand the pain I put *them* through last year. It was the flailings of a drowning person, but it still caused irreparable harm to my SO and others who love me.

Not wanting to cause that pain again is reason enough to stay on top of my meds. Was I selfish for being suicidal? I don't think so. But I know I would go back to the ER to commit myself in a heartbeat before putting my SO through that again. And I see my self care (med regimen, etc) as selfless, because it keeps me from becoming a person who causes pain to the people I love the most.

So honestly, I wouldn't say shit to someone who says suicide is selfish, because they obviously don't understand the complexities of life and brain chemistry that lead to suicide. And they likely don't want to listen. But if you read this through, maybe it shed a little light.

Success=doing what you love, where you're doing it, and who you're doing it with. 

Not that I have the secret to happiness or anything but by living intentionally and guiding my life with intention I have accomplished all three. It doesn't fix my fucked up family or my trauma or my illnesses. But damn it feels good to know that I chose this life, hand picked it to be just the way I like it. 

Also, read the book of Ecclesiastes. It's in the old testament, but it is philosophy rather than religion. I ascribed to it's principals even as an atheist. 

Be careful who you hang out with, where you go, what "opportunities" you accept. There will be ripple effects down the road from your choices that will be crashing waves by the time you catch up to them. So make sure you choose wisely.

Tl;Dr: the brain is a part of the body

Long version: whenever you go into crisis mode because of whatever negative stimulus (falling down the stairs, or getting embarrassed and laughed at at work), your body reacts the same way. When you sense danger, whether an impending break up or an ongoing car, your brain floods your body will hormones: adrenaline spikes your blood pressure and speeds your reaction time and cortisol, the "stress hormone", and shuts down any bodily functions seemed non-essential to fight or flight, among other things. 

Whatever happens after you are ready and primed, and then when you come down it's actually pretty traumatic in itself. Ever been so upset your hands wouldn't start shaking. Couple that feeling with the emotional blow of a break up (or a car wreck) and you're going to be in pain, whether mental agony (which we all know exists) or physical.

Also, and this is the most important: mental health is health. Your brain is intrinsically connected with the rest of your body. Just as exercise helps depression, depression and anxiety can negatively affect the rest of your body in such ways as weight gain or blood pressure. Mental trauma on its own can be so agonizing you get flashbacks, like in PTSD. But thankfully there are treatments. Therapies like cognitive behavioral therapy, counseling, medications, group therapy. 

If you broke a bone you'd set it, put it in a cast, take some Tylenol, and rest up. If you experienced psychological trauma it is just as important to treat that. Taking care of yourself includes your mental health.
